About twelve million years ago, northeastern Nebraska had a waterhole,

Being the biggest animal at the waterhole only meant waiting the longest.

Wasps Inside Fossil Flies.
In the late eighteen hundreds, phosphate miners in the Quercy region of southern France
kept digging up thousands of tiny fossil fly pupae.
A pupa is the stage where a fly rebuilds itself inside a hard little case,
and these ones had turned to stone somewhere between thirty-four and forty million years ago.
Each was about three millimeters long, less than half the length of a grain of long-grain rice.
From the outside, they looked like exactly what they were, which was flies.
In twenty eighteen, a team of German researchers put fifteen hundred and ten of them
through a synchrotron, an X-ray source powerful enough to see inside the stone without breaking it open.
Here's what the scan found.
In fifty-five of those pupae, there was no fly left at all.
There was a wasp instead, a parasitoid wasp.
A female laid her egg inside the developing fly,
and the young wasp grew up by eating its host from the inside until only the case was left.
Most of them were preserved as adults, still sitting in the case.
The team described four new species,
and the most common one is named Xenomorphia resurrecta,
after the creature in the Alien films that develops inside its host the same way.
These wasps hunted fly pupae,
which is exactly why Doug is dressed as one,
and he has been told to hold still and think like a pupa.
For forty million years, they looked like flies,

The Snake in the Nest.
In nineteen eighty-four, a geologist named Dhananjay Mohabey was collecting dinosaur eggs in Gujarat, in western India,

A colleague recognized that they belonged to a snake a few years later,

In two thousand one, a visiting paleontologist looked at the slab again,

The Dinosaur Biter.
For a long time, the mammals of the dinosaur age were imagined as small, nocturnal, and mostly on the menu.
The Lujiatun beds disagree.
